title: Counter-Selector Wave 39: digest-selected new-pod restore and explicit dependency replay
purpose: Adjudicate one observed public checkpoint control in which the destination create request selects an OCI checkpoint image by repository digest and starts a restored successor in a new pod, while separately preserving application continuation with explicit bind-mount replay and an inspectable registry-push route without combining package variants or systems.

complete_portable_operational_handoff_re: one same object and transition boundary are identified
one fixed public package digest is retained and selected by the destination
every operational entry is itemized with integrity and semantic role
the recipient acknowledges the exact package inventory and authority state
credentials dependencies access open decisions deadlines and rollback state travel with the package
the destination is demonstrably clean of undeclared predecessor state and hidden environmental borrowing
application-specific successor operation is observed from the exact acknowledged digest
registry transport and destination acquisition are receipted when claimed
an external independent verifier reproduces the entire package-to-operation chain

controls.public_label: repository-digest-selected checkpoint image restored into a new pod

source_records.title: Checkpoint OCI image restore using repoDigest
source_records.artifact_scope: Checkpoints a running container, removes the source container and pod, builds an OCI checkpoint image, resolves its repoDigest, creates a new pod using that digest as the requested image, creates the restored container, and starts it.

source_records.title: CRI-O checkpoint image recognition and restore implementation
source_records.artifact_scope: Resolves the requested image, recognizes the checkpoint annotation, mounts the exact storage image, rejects unsupported namespaced signature-policy restore, pins RootfsImageRef when present, requires declared bind mounts, and constructs the successor in the destination sandbox.

source_records.title: CRI-O checkpoint image annotation contract
source_records.artifact_scope: Defines checkpoint image annotations for original container name, raw and resolved rootfs image identity, CRI-O version, and CRIU version.

source_records.title: OCI content descriptor contract
source_records.artifact_scope: Defines digest-and-size content descriptors, content addressability, and independent digest verification for referenced bytes.

source_records.title: OCI image manifest contract
source_records.artifact_scope: Defines one image manifest with content-addressed configuration and ordered layer descriptors.

components.same_object_identity: The checkpoint archive preserves the source container state; the test removes the source container and pod before creating and starting a successor from the checkpoint image in a new pod.
components.checkpoint_package_identity: A scratch OCI image contains the exported checkpoint archive and the CRI-O checkpoint-name annotation.
components.exact_package_selector: The test asks CRI-O for the image repoDigest and places that digest, not merely the tag, into the destination container ImageSpec.
components.package_content_addressing: The repository digest selects one OCI manifest whose config and layers are addressed by digest and size.
components.internal_inventory_and_entry_integrity: The outer OCI graph is content-addressed, but the checkpoint layer has no recipient-acknowledged per-entry manifest covering every operational file and semantic role.
components.outgoing_and_incoming_roles: The outgoing CRI-O checkpoint path emits the archive and checkpoint image; the incoming CRI-O create/restore path recognizes, mounts, and restores the image.
components.destination_boundary: The source container and pod are removed, then a new pod is created. The test does not establish a new host, empty image store, independent administrator, or clean external environment.
components.authority_and_credentials: The destination create request supplies pod, labels, annotations, security context, and mounts; no complete credential, secret, signing, recipient-rights, or authority ledger travels as one acknowledged inventory.
components.dependencies_and_access: RootfsImageRef is used when present to avoid silently pulling a changed tag, but compatible CRI-O, OCI runtime, CRIU, kernel, storage, cgroup, network, image store, and mount state remain external dependencies.
components.open_decisions_and_deadlines: Destination pod metadata, resources, security context, mounts, and invocation choices remain create-request state rather than one package-carried decision and deadline ledger.
components.rollback_safe_decline_and_failure_contai: Missing image, unsupported namespaced signature policy, missing metadata, missing mounts, stopped sandbox, and restore failures stop the path; no same-package rollback restores the removed source pod.
components.recipient_or_successor_acknowledgment: The successor runtime consumes the repoDigest-selected image sufficiently to create and start a container, but does not enumerate and sign every package entry, dependency, authority, and open decision.
components.successor_operation_from_package: The destination create request names the repoDigest, the restored container is created in the new pod, and crictl starts it.
components.independent_verification: The behavior is covered by public project integration tests and implementation review; no external institution reproduces the exact digest-selected package-to-operation chain.

positive_findings: The exact restore request uses the dynamically resolved repository digest rather than relying only on a mutable image tag.
The source container and source pod are removed before the destination pod is created.
The checkpoint image is recognized by an explicit checkpoint annotation and mounted by resolved storage image ID.
RootfsImageRef, when present, prevents a later mutable tag from silently selecting a different base image.
A new-pod successor is created and started from the digest-selected checkpoint image.
known_limits: The test does not retain one literal checkpoint repoDigest value as a durable public receipt; it computes and consumes a runtime value.
The image is already in the local image store; no push, pull, registry-recipient, or cross-host round trip is exercised in the exact repoDigest test.
A new pod is not proof of a clean host, empty image store, independent administrator, or absence of hidden predecessor state.
The exact repoDigest test starts the restored sleeper but does not assert application-specific output, semantic correctness, or data-plane continuation.
The outer OCI manifest does not itemize and semantically bind every file inside the checkpoint archive layer.
The restore path still depends on a compatible rootfs image, runtime, CRIU, kernel, cgroup, storage, network, and destination configuration.
Namespaced signature-policy validation is explicitly unsupported for container restore.
No recipient acknowledges an exact operational inventory and no external party independently reproduces the chain.
The result is a system-control receipt and not person-level operator evidence.

controls.public_label: new-pod archive restore with application output and explicit bind-mount replay
controls.system_or_subject: CRI-O checkpoint archive restore with bind mounts

source_records.title: Checkpoint archive restore with log growth and mount re-declaration
source_records.artifact_scope: Records pre-checkpoint log content, removes source container and pod, proves create fails when required bind mounts are omitted, re-declares the mounts, starts the restored container in a new pod, verifies restored status, preserved prior output, and subsequent log-line growth.

source_records.title: CRI-O restore dependency reconstruction and refusal rules
source_records.artifact_scope: Reconstructs destination container configuration, pins RootfsImageRef when available, ignores platform-generated mounts, requires every other bind mount in the create request, and refuses stopped sandboxes or unresolved dependencies.

source_records.title: CRI-O archive and OCI restore failure fixtures
source_records.artifact_scope: Exercises invalid identity, running-container refusal, invalid config, archive restore failure, OCI-image mount paths, and the minimal CRIU inventory requirement.

components.same_object_identity: The test preserves the source workload log history across checkpoint, source removal, new-pod creation, and restored execution.
components.checkpoint_package_identity: A checkpoint tar archive is passed directly as the destination image input.
components.exact_package_selector: The path identifies one local archive file but is not a repository-digest selector and does not publish a fixed content digest.
components.package_content_addressing: No OCI manifest or committed digest binds this exact archive in the test.
components.internal_inventory_and_entry_integrity: The archive contains checkpoint state, but the recipient does not acknowledge a complete per-entry digest and semantic-role inventory.
components.outgoing_and_incoming_roles: The source CRI-O checkpoint path exports the archive; the destination CRI-O create/restore path unpacks metadata and restores the successor.
components.destination_boundary: The source container and pod are removed and a new pod is created on the same test environment.
components.authority_and_credentials: Destination mounts, labels, annotations, resources, and security context are re-supplied through the create request; no complete package-carried authority or credential ledger is acknowledged.
components.dependencies_and_access: The first create attempt fails because required host bind mounts are absent. Re-declaring those external host paths makes the dependency visible and allows restore.
components.open_decisions_and_deadlines: The create request supplies destination choices and host paths outside the archive rather than receiving one complete package decision ledger.
components.rollback_safe_decline_and_failure_contai: Missing bind mounts fail closed before successful create; no same-package rollback restores the deleted source pod after a later failure.
components.recipient_or_successor_acknowledgment: CRI-O marks the container restored and accepts re-declared dependencies, but does not sign an itemized package inventory.
components.successor_operation_from_package: The restored workload retains prior log content and produces additional lines after restore.
components.independent_verification: The receipt is an originating-project integration test rather than external independent reproduction.

positive_findings: The source container and pod are removed before a new destination pod is created.
Omitting required bind mounts causes the destination create request to fail.
Re-declaring the exact mount destinations permits restore, making one external dependency class explicit.
The restored flag is true, prior output remains visible, and the line count grows after restore.
RootfsImageRef can preserve the exact base-image identity instead of following a changed mutable tag.
known_limits: The exact archive is not selected by OCI repoDigest or another frozen public content identifier.
The host bind-mount paths are supplied outside the package and therefore prove dependency replay rather than package self-containment.
The new pod remains in the same test environment and does not establish a clean host or independent recipient.
The package lacks a complete per-entry digest and semantic-role manifest.
No recipient acknowledges credentials, authorities, dependencies, decisions, deadlines, and rollback state as one inventory.
Same-project integration tests are not external independent reproduction.
The application receipt belongs to the archive variant and cannot be borrowed into the repoDigest OCI-image control.
The result is not person support or field-test authority.

controls.public_label: inspectable checkpoint archive converted to registry-pushable OCI image without downstream operation receipt

source_records.title: checkpointctl checkpoint inspection and OCI build route
source_records.artifact_scope: Shows high-level and tree inspection of checkpoint archives and documents conversion to an OCI image followed by buildah push to a registry.

source_records.title: checkpointctl build command
source_records.artifact_scope: Defines the command that converts one checkpoint archive into an OCI-compatible image and presents buildah push as the next transport step.

source_records.title: checkpointctl OCI image builder implementation
source_records.artifact_scope: Creates a scratch image, adds the checkpoint archive, extracts spec and config metadata for annotations, and commits the image.

components.same_object_identity: The tool inspects or converts a named checkpoint archive; no downstream same-object successor receipt is part of the build route.
components.checkpoint_package_identity: One archive can be shown, inspected, added to a scratch image, annotated, committed, and offered for registry push.
components.exact_package_selector: The examples use an image tag and do not retain a fixed pushed digest or downstream restore request.
components.package_content_addressing: The committed OCI image will be content-addressed by the image system, but the documented route does not preserve the resulting digest in a package-to-operation receipt.
components.internal_inventory_and_entry_integrity: show and inspect expose container, image, runtime, network, process, memory, and rootfs information, while the builder adds the archive as a layer and extracts selected annotations; it does not create a recipient-signed per-entry digest ledger.
components.outgoing_and_incoming_roles: checkpointctl is an inspector and image producer; buildah is the documented registry pusher. No receiving restore runtime is joined in the same receipt.
components.destination_boundary: A registry destination is named as a route, not observed as a restore and operation destination.
components.authority_and_credentials: Registry and runtime credentials, package authority, recipient rights, and destination policy are not carried in an acknowledged operational inventory.
components.dependencies_and_access: buildah, registry access, compatible restore runtime, rootfs image, CRIU, kernel, and destination configuration remain external.
components.open_decisions_and_deadlines: Image naming, registry, deployment, restore, and rollback choices remain outside the generated image receipt.
components.rollback_safe_decline_and_failure_contai: Builder failures stop image creation and temporary build containers are removed, but there is no downstream package restore or rollback receipt.
components.recipient_or_successor_acknowledgment: Neither registry push documentation nor package inspection is an operational recipient inventory acknowledgment.
components.successor_operation_from_package: No successor operation from the exact built and pushed image is demonstrated by these sources.
components.independent_verification: The tooling is public and testable, but the full build-push-restore-operation chain is not externally reproduced.

positive_findings: Checkpoint archives can be inspected for high-level identity, runtime, network, process, memory, and rootfs state.
One archive can be converted into an OCI-compatible image with checkpoint annotations.
The documented route explicitly supports pushing the resulting image to a registry.
The builder removes its temporary build container on completion or failure.
known_limits: Inspection is not a signed or recipient-acknowledged inventory.
The builder adds the archive as one layer and extracts selected annotations rather than emitting a complete per-entry digest and semantic-role manifest.
The documented push route does not preserve one actual pushed digest in the source receipt.
No downstream runtime restores and operates from the exact built image in the same evidence chain.
Registry, credential, policy, rootfs, runtime, CRIU, kernel, and destination dependencies remain external.
No external independent party reproduces the complete route.
The route cannot be combined with CRI-O or Podman operation receipts from a different package instance.

next_action: Seek one fixed-digest checkpoint image that is pushed and acquired at a demonstrably clean destination, carries an itemized integrity-bound operational inventory including external dependencies and authority state, receives explicit recipient acknowledgment, demonstrates application-specific continuation from that exact digest, supports rollback or safe decline, and is reproduced by an external independent party. Do not borrow the CRI-O archive application receipt, checkpointctl inspection route, Podman operation, E2B live continuity, or Cargo proof across package instances.
